# Copilot Instructions

- Compiled `.mo` files are committed to the repo under `locale/`. When you edit a `.po` file you must also regenerate its `.mo` counterpart by running `python manage.py compilemessages` inside the web container (`docker exec hospital_dwh_web_dev python manage.py compilemessages`), then commit both files together. If the container is not running, start it first with `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d db web` and wait for it to be healthy. The container startup script (`docker/startup.py`) also does this automatically on deploy when it detects the `.po` is newer than the `.mo`. The check script (`scripts/check-translations.sh`) enforces that `.mo` files are present and up to date.
- Never add inline `<script>` blocks with JavaScript logic to HTML templates. Instead, put all JavaScript in a dedicated static file under `warehouse/static/js/` and load it with `<script src="{% static 'js/filename.js' %}">`. The only exception is `<script type="application/json">` data islands used to pass Django template variables to external JS files, and the Tailwind CDN config script in `_tailwind_config.html` which must remain inline.
- Put all static images (SVG, PNG, JPEG, ICO, WebP) under `warehouse/static/img/` and reference them in templates with `<img src="{% static 'img/filename.ext' %}">`. Never place image assets in the project root or outside the `warehouse/static/` hierarchy.
- Every user-facing string in templates must be wrapped with `{% trans "…" %}` (or `{% blocktrans %}…{% endblocktrans %}` for multi-word/variable interpolation). After adding new strings, run `python manage.py compilemessages` inside the web container, add translations to both `locale/cs/LC_MESSAGES/django.po` and `locale/en/LC_MESSAGES/django.po`, recompile, and commit all `.po` + `.mo` files together. Strings passed from templates to JavaScript must use the `json_script` data-island pattern so the translated value is available to JS without inline scripting.
- Always use MOU colour tokens for any UI work — never introduce arbitrary hex values or Tailwind default palette colours. The canonical tokens are defined in `warehouse/templates/includes/_tailwind_config.html` and are: `mou-cyan` (#53c0d7), `mou-orange` (#f04600), `mou-blue` (#007fc8), `mou-dark` (#1a2332), `mou-yellow` (#fbeebc), `mou-cyan-light` / `mou-cyan-border`, `mou-orange-light` / `mou-orange-border`, `mou-blue-light` / `mou-blue-border`, `page-bg` (#f8f9fa), `outer-bg` (#eef2f7), `site-border` (#e5e7eb), `layer1` / `layer1-border`, `layer2` / `layer2-border`, `txt` (#374151), `txt-muted` (#4b5563). When these tokens are not available (e.g. in JS canvas drawing or inline styles), use the raw hex values from this list.
- Before creating any new HTML, always check `warehouse/templates/` for an existing template or include that already provides the needed structure (e.g. cards, modals, tables, form rows, alert banners). Reuse it via `{% extends %}` or `{% include %}` rather than duplicating markup. When adding a new UI pattern that will be used in more than one place, extract it into a reusable partial under `warehouse/templates/includes/` so it is not repeated. Never copy-paste blocks of markup between templates — factor shared markup into an include instead.
- Follow a strict **layered architecture** — views (UI layer) must never make direct ORM queries or import Django models. All database access must go through service classes:
  - **Warehouse app**: use `WarehouseMetadataService` (`warehouse/services.py`) for all `metadata_db` and `fair_genomes_db` queries (tables, columns, stat charts, column filters). Use `UnifiedCatalogService` (`shared/services.py`) for cross-database dataset/distribution aggregation.
  - **Ticketing app**: use `TicketingService` (`ticketing/services/ticketing_service.py`) for ticket creation, submission, and history queries. Use `CartService` (`ticketing/cart.py`) for session-based cart operations.
  - **Views may only** import from service modules, DTOs (`shared/dtos.py`), export helpers (`shared/export.py`), and cart utilities — never from `*.models` directly.
  - **Admin files and management commands** are exempt from this rule — they may use direct ORM access and model imports.
  - When adding new database queries, add a method to the appropriate service class rather than querying in the view. Service methods should return plain Python data structures (dicts, lists, dataclasses), not QuerySets.
- After making any code changes, run the full quality check suite via `./scripts/check.sh` (or `./scripts/check.sh --check` for CI-style dry-run). This runs linting (Ruff), formatting (Ruff), type checking (mypy), security scanning (Bandit), translation completeness, and the test suite. Fix all reported issues before considering the task complete. Individual checks can also be run separately: `scripts/check-lint.sh`, `scripts/check-format.sh`, `scripts/check-types.sh`, `scripts/check-security.sh`, `scripts/check-translations.sh`, `scripts/check-tests.sh`. Tests can also be run inside the container with `docker exec hospital_dwh_web_dev python manage.py test`.
